pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #1 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why do we keep a class portfolio of songs? (1 mark)
   A. To sell them
   B. To hide them
   C. To throw them away
   D. So the songs are kept safe and are not forgotten

2. Which action shows attentive listening? (1 mark)
   A. Drawing on your desk
   B. Talking to a friend
   C. Looking out of the window
   D. Looking at the speaker and staying quiet

3. What is the plural of the English word mango? (1 mark)
   A. mangoies
   B. mangos'
   C. mangoss
   D. mangoes

4. Which is a clue that a noun is plural? (1 mark)
   A. A full stop
   B. A capital letter
   C. The word the
   D. A number word such as three before it

5. Where should you look to check an answer to a comprehension question? (1 mark)
   A. In another book only
   B. At the ceiling
   C. Back at the text
   D. In your imagination only

6. What should you leave between two words? (1 mark)
   A. A whole line
   B. A picture
   C. No space
   D. A finger space

7. Which pencil grip is best? (1 mark)
   A. Grip it with a fist
   B. Hold it by the end with your teeth
   C. Press it very hard
   D. Hold it lightly between the thumb and first finger

8. A verb is (1 mark)
   A. a word that describes a colour
   B. a word that shows an action
   C. a word that names a person
   D. a joining word

9. Which sentence uses a signal word for the last step? (1 mark)
   A. First, wait.
   B. Then, wait.
   C. Finally, wait until the rain stops.
   D. Next, wait.

10. In English, what usually happens to the voice at the end of a question? (1 mark)
   A. It stays exactly the same always
   B. It becomes a whisper
   C. It falls to silence
   D. It rises

11. What does reading with expression mean? (1 mark)
   A. Showing feeling in your voice as you read
   B. Reading in a flat voice
   C. Reading without stopping
   D. Reading in whispers

12. Which sentence ends correctly? (1 mark)
   A. The sun is hot:
   B. The sun is hot,
   C. The sun is hot?
   D. The sun is hot.

13. Where should commas go in: We planted maize beans peas and kale? (1 mark)
   A. After planted
   B. After We
   C. After maize and beans
   D. After kale

14. What is the guessing language game with verbs? (1 mark)
   A. Pupils act a verb and others guess it
   B. Pupils read a book
   C. Pupils sing nouns
   D. Pupils write verbs on the board silently

15. What should you do if you did not hear a question? (1 mark)
   A. Leave
   B. Guess loudly
   C. Politely ask for it to be repeated
   D. Laugh

16. In a written dialogue the speaker's name usually comes (1 mark)
   A. in the middle of a word
   B. on a different page
   C. at the end
   D. at the start of the line

17. How are words arranged in a dictionary? (1 mark)
   A. In alphabetical order
   B. By the number of letters
   C. By size of the word
   D. By colour

18. In The road was congested and the matatu could not move, what does congested mean? (1 mark)
   A. Very clean
   B. Very short
   C. Very wide
   D. Very crowded

19. What can you use to practise reordering sentences? (1 mark)
   A. Nothing
   B. Cut strips and arrange them
   C. A bucket
   D. A hammer

20. What is the main idea of a paragraph? (1 mark)
   A. What the paragraph is mostly about
   B. The title font
   C. The number of lines
   D. The last word

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. List three ways of reading with expression. (3 marks)

22. Name four question words used to check comprehension. (2 marks)

23. Explain what to do when you get a small burn and why. (4 marks)

24. Complete each sentence with a suitable verb: (a) We ______ our hands before eating. (b) Please ______ the door. (3 marks)

25. Play the role of the soloist in a singing game. Write three short instructions you would sing and say what the group should do for each. (5 marks)

26. Explain how to take part in a class handwriting gallery walk. (4 marks)

27. Explain what intonation is and give one English example of a rising voice. (2 marks)

28. Pick out the nouns in this song line: We roast the maize and boil the beans. (3 marks)

29. Describe how a group can read a text aloud together and give feedback. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #1 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — So the songs are kept safe and are not forgotten
   A portfolio preserves the songs collected from the community.

2. D — Looking at the speaker and staying quiet
   Attentive listening means giving your eyes, ears and mind to the speaker.

3. D — mangoes
   Mango takes es in the plural, mangoes.

4. D — A number word such as three before it
   Number words show how many there are.

5. C — Back at the text
   Good readers go back to the text.

6. D — A finger space
   A finger width keeps words clear.

7. D — Hold it lightly between the thumb and first finger
   A light grip prevents tiredness.

8. B — a word that shows an action
   Verbs show what is done.

9. C — Finally, wait until the rain stops.
   Finally shows the last step.

10. D — It rises
   Many questions end with a rising voice.

11. A — Showing feeling in your voice as you read
   Expression shows the feelings in the text.

12. D — The sun is hot.
   A statement ends with a full stop.

13. C — After maize and beans
   The list is maize, beans, peas and kale.

14. A — Pupils act a verb and others guess it
   Acting helps everyone connect verbs with actions.

15. C — Politely ask for it to be repeated
   Asking politely helps you answer correctly.

16. D — at the start of the line
   The name shows who speaks.

17. A — In alphabetical order
   Dictionaries use alphabetical order.

18. D — Very crowded
   The matatu could not move because there was too much traffic.

19. B — Cut strips and arrange them
   Strips of sentences can be moved into order.

20. A — What the paragraph is mostly about
   The main idea is the central point.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Change loudness, change speed, pause at punctuation, use different voices for characters, use face and hands.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each way.

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: Who, what, where, when, why, how (any four).
   Working / marking points: One mark for two correct question words and two marks for four.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: Put it under cool running water for several minutes to reduce pain, cover it with a clean cloth and tell an adult or go to a clinic.
   Working / marking points: One mark each for cool water, the reason, clean cover and telling an adult.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: wash (or clean) and close (or shut)
   Working / marking points: One mark for each suitable verb and one mark for correct spelling.

25. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any three clear instructions with matching actions, for example Clap two times (the group claps twice), Stir the pot (the group pretends to stir), Turn around (the group turns).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each clear instruction and one mark for each matching response, with a total of five marks for three well matched pairs and correct listening steps.

26. (4 marks)
   Answer: Write your best sentence on a strip. Display it on the wall. Walk quietly, look at each strip, and leave a kind and helpful comment.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four points.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: Intonation is the rise and fall of the voice as we speak. A question such as Are you coming? rises at the end.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one mark for a correct example.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: maize and beans (and we is a pronoun, not a noun)
   Working / marking points: One mark for maize, one mark for beans, and one mark for not including roast or boil, which are actions.

29. (4 marks)
   Answer: Read silently first, help each other with hard words, take turns to read, then listen to the group and give one good point and one point to improve in a kind way.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four correct parts.
